claim: The invention of patent US2292387A relates broadly to secret communication systems involving the use of carrier waves of different frequencies, and is especially useful in the remote control of dirigible craft, such as torpedoes.

evidence.quote: US2292387A - Secret communication system - Google Patents

This invention relates broadly to secret communication systems involving the use of carrier waves of different frequencies, and is especially useful in the remote control of dirigible craft, such as torpedoes.

notes: Patent text as reproduced by Google Patents.

claim: In the system of patent US2292387A, a pair of synchronous records, one at the transmitting station and one at the receiving station, change the tuning of the transmitting and receiving apparatus from time to time, so that without knowledge of the records an enemy would be unable to determine at what frequency a controlling impulse would be sent.

evidence.quote: US2292387A - Secret communication system - Google Patents

Briefly, our system as adapted for radio control of a. remote craft, employs a pair of synchronous records, one at the transmitting station and one at the receiving station, which change the tuning of the transmitting and receiving apparatus from time to time, so that without knowledge of the records an enemy would be unable to determine at what frequency a controlling impulse would be sent.

notes: Patent text as reproduced by Google Patents (frequency hopping mechanism).

claim: Patent US2292387A contemplates employing records of the type used in player pianos; a conventional player piano record may have 88 rows of perforations, which would permit the use of 88 different carrier frequencies.

evidence.quote: US2292387A - Secret communication system - Google Patents

Furthermore, we contemplate employing records of the type used for many years in player pianos, and which consist, of long rolls of paper having perforations variously positioned in a. plurality of longitudinal rows along the records. In a conventional player piano record there may be 88 rows of perforations, and in our system such a record would permit the use of 88 different carrier frequencies

notes: Patent text as reproduced by Google Patents.

claim: The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) honored former movie actress Hedy Lamarr with a special award on March 12, 1997, in Burlingame, CA, for her co-invention of spread-spectrum broadcast communications technologies.

evidence.quote: Burlingame, CA - March 12, 1997 - In what the organization\'s spokesman describes as "a unique event both for EFF and for the Computers, Freedom, and Privacy conference," the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) will honor former movie actress Hedy Lamarr with a special award this evening for her co-invention of spread-spectrum broadcast communications technologies.

notes: EFF media release of 11-12 March 1997 announcing that evening's ceremony; the release is dated the day of the award. The award is called a special award; the 1997 Pioneer Awards themselves went to Johan Helsingius and Marc Rotenberg (see the next fact). The IHH page says she won the EFF Pioneer Award; tmp-domain-S-7 (Florida Inventors Hall of Fame) also says Pioneer Award. Conflict for review.

claim: Lamarr was honored along with Johan Helsingius of Finland, and Marc Rotenberg of Washington, D.C., whose work for civil liberties on the Net earned them each a 1997 Pioneer Award.

evidence.quote: Lamarr will be honored along with Johan Helsingius of Finland, and Marc Rotenberg of Washington, D.C., whose work for civil liberties on the Net has earned them each a 1997 Pioneer Award.
Two individuals were named recipients of this year\'s Pioneer award; they are Johan ("Julf") Helsingius

notes: Per the EFF release, the two 1997 Pioneer Award recipients were Helsingius and Rotenberg; Lamarr (with George Antheil) received a special award. Bears on the IHH claim that she won the EFF Pioneer Award (1997).
